title: Peace for the Nations, Pride Brought Low
overview: Isaiah sets a hopeful picture of a future when all nations learn God's ways and give up war beside a blunt warning that Judah's pride, wealth and idols will be humbled.

parts.label: Nations stream to Jerusalem (vv. 1-4)
parts.note: Isaiah pictures a future when Jerusalem's temple hill is raised above every other mountain, and people from every nation come there to learn God's ways. God settles their disputes, and they hammer their swords into farm tools because no one trains for war anymore.

parts.label: What Judah is really like (vv. 5-9)
parts.note: After inviting his people to live by God's light, Isaiah lists why God has left them: fortune telling borrowed from neighbors, piles of gold and war horses, and idols made by their own hands. Israel's law warned kings against hoarding gold and horses, and the section ends with a harsh line asking God not to forgive them, which may be a prayer or a grim prediction.

parts.label: A day against all pride (vv. 10-18)
parts.note: That day is a coming time when God steps in to judge. Tall cedars and oaks, high hills, towers, city walls and great trading ships stand for everything people boast in or hide behind, and all of it will be brought down so that only God stands high.

parts.label: Running for the caves (vv. 19-21)
parts.note: When God rises to shake the earth, people flee into caves, as people in that hilly land did when armies came. They throw their costly silver and gold idols to the moles and bats, admitting at last that these were worth nothing.

parts.label: Stop leaning on people (v. 22)
parts.note: The chapter ends by telling readers to stop putting their ultimate trust in human beings. People are fragile, with only a breath in their nostrils, so they make a poor foundation.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether the peaceful scene in verses 2 to 4 is fulfilled spiritually through the spread of Christian faith among the nations or still awaits a literal future in which Jerusalem becomes the world's center and war truly ends.
think: What do people today rely on for security in the way Judah relied on gold, horses and high walls, and how well does it actually hold up?
